question: A hotel booking page, in the style Britain's regulator examined in 2019. What do the urgent lines really say?
answer: Mostly how much they want you to hurry. In 2019 Britain's Competition and Markets Authority found claims like these could give a false impression of how scarce rooms were: a last room could be only that site's last room, and those looking might want other dates. Six large booking sites agreed to change.
move: Urgency claimed by the seller is a sales tool until proven otherwise.
ask: When a site tells me to hurry, what happens if I simply close it and come back tomorrow?

scene.head: Hotel booking site
scene.title: Seafront hotel, 2 nights
scene.body: Only 1 room left. 14 people are looking at this hotel right now. Booked 9 times in the last 24 hours. This price is held for 10 minutes.

phrases.plain: Our site's last room of this type
phrases.why: The CMA found it could mean the last room this site had, not the last in the hotel.

phrases.text: 14 people are looking at this hotel
phrases.plain: Others are browsing, perhaps for other dates
phrases.why: Counts of other viewers can include people searching completely different nights.

phrases.text: This price is held for 10 minutes
phrases.plain: We'd like you to decide before you compare
phrases.why: A countdown makes checking elsewhere feel risky. Regulators count it as pressure selling.

scene.ask: One line can be true and still mislead. Which?
scene.watch: Urgency the seller creates is a sales tool. Ask what happens if you wait a day.

source: Competition and Markets Authority, online hotel booking
